Dana: Heads-up — Helios asked for a short POC next Tue. They need steady-run numbers, microburst behavior, and an explicit multi-AZ cost delta. Also a short security Q pack. Can we draft the plan?
Marco: Sure. What steady qps and model? Region?
Dana: Steady target 900 qps, microbursts to 2800 qps for ~7s, model is an 11B chat, avg prompt 35 tokens / avg response 500 tokens -> ~535 tokens per call. Region: us-west primary with multi-AZ failover.
Yuki: Proposed test sequence:
- 10m ramp to 900 qps
- 50m steady at 900 qps (collect p50/p95/p99, GPU util, queue depth, KV cache hit rate)
- 5 bursts at 2800 qps for 7s spaced 9m apart
- 15m cooldown
Run both fp16 and 4-bit quant bundles; capture kernel counters and soft-eviction events.
Rita: Ops snippet to paste into runbook:

```
# loadgen
--target-qps 900
--ramp 600s
--steady 3000s
--burst "2800:7s x5"
--samples ./helios-samples.json
--metrics http://prom-prom:9090/metrics
```

Marco: Quick staging numbers (A100-equivalent, warm): fp16 steady 920 qps, p95=140ms, p99=310ms, KV-hit ~79%. During bursts we observed transient queueing with p99 peaking ~640ms until soft-eviction smoothed tail.
Yuki: 4-bit quant run shows ~2.1x throughput (sustained ~1930 qps) but worst-case p99 increases by ~1.5x during bursts. Note trade-off in deck.
Marco: For hosted vs dedicated note: hosted multi-tenant variance typically adds ~25% to tail figures; recommend dedicated reserved for strict p99 SLAs. Also recommend enabling prefix KV cache and soft-eviction to reduce tail.
PricingBot: Ballpark cost sketch: hosted example $0.47 per 1k tokens -> per request ~ $0.251. Dedicated reserved estimate to sustain 900 qps with headroom: approx $2.3k/day amortized. Active-active multi-AZ failover ~ +33% infra cost.
Dana: Please turn those into a one-pager (run plan, quick results, two pricing scenarios, and security bullets).
Rita: Security draft notes: CMK support (customer-managed keys), PrivateLink/VPC peering for Private deployments, audit log export to SIEM, SOC2 Type II attestation available. On-prem appliance pathway: 4-8 weeks typical.
Marco: Ops recommendation addendum: to hit p99 <350ms at 900 qps use Dedicated + reserved capacity, enable prefix caching, prewarm 30m, and consider truncating long responses.
Yuki: Also add note that soft-eviction on KV cache reduced p99 by ~26% in our staging runs — useful during bursts.
Dana: Thanks all. Can we review the deck Fri 9:30am PT? I want to send the charter by EOD Mon.
